<!--
  THE AGENT'S JOB DESCRIPTION — editable capability text, same as prompt.md.

  Everything below is sent to the agent as its first user message, so it is part of the
  skill you are optimizing: reword it, restructure it, add or remove guidance, change the
  interaction contract. This comment block is STRIPPED before the agent sees it.

  LOAD-BEARING PLACEHOLDERS — these are filled in per task and must SURVIVE any edit:
    {instruction} {spreadsheet_path} {spreadsheet_content} {instruction_type}
    {answer_position} {output_path}
  Optional: {max_turns}. No other {braces} are allowed.

  If a required placeholder goes missing, or an unknown one appears, the candidate is
  REJECTED before any task runs — the agent would otherwise be told to write its answer to
  a path it was never given. A literal brace must be doubled: {{ or }}.
-->
You need to solve the following spreadsheet manipulation question. It contains six pieces of information:
- instruction: the question about spreadsheet manipulation.
- spreadsheet_path: the path of the spreadsheet file you need to manipulate.
- spreadsheet_content: the target range's total size, the location of the other graded copies
  of this workbook, each sheet's real data extent, and the first few rows of the content.
- instruction_type: Cell-Level Manipulation (answer_position is exact cell(s)) or Sheet-Level Manipulation (answer_position is the maximum range you may modify).
- answer_position: the cell(s)/range you must modify or fill in.
- output_path: write the modified spreadsheet file to this exact path.

### instruction
{instruction}

### spreadsheet_path
{spreadsheet_path}

### spreadsheet_content
{spreadsheet_content}

### instruction_type
{instruction_type}

### answer_position
{answer_position}

### output_path
{output_path}

You have up to {max_turns} rounds of interaction. Each reply must contain EXACTLY ONE Python
code block, fenced exactly like this (triple backticks + the word python), with nothing else
dressed around the code:

```python
# your code here
print(result)
```

Do NOT wrap your code in `<tool_call>`, XML, JSON, or `call:` markers — ONLY a triple-backtick
```python fence is executed. If a round comes back saying "no python code block was found",
your previous reply was not fenced correctly: re-send the SAME code inside a ```python fence.

Work in this order, one code block per round:
1. INSPECT: open spreadsheet_path and print the exact cells/columns you need — and, for
   Sheet-Level tasks, any sample or expected-result data the instruction refers to — so your
   logic is based on the real data, not the preview alone.
2. SOLVE: write the modified workbook to output_path.
3. VERIFY (required before you finish): re-open output_path and, for the cells in
   answer_position, print each value AND its Python type. You may finish ONLY after confirming
   ALL of the following:
   - every target cell holds the intended value — none left empty/None, and none left at 0 or
     a default from a failed lookup;
   - numbers are stored as numbers, and dates/times as real date/time values (not strings);
   - a sanity check holds — e.g. a filtered total is not ~0 when many rows should match, and
     the number of rows/cells written matches the expected extent of answer_position.
   If any check fails, fix the code and write again — and never resubmit a code block
   identical to one that already ran.

Reply with NO code block only once the verification above has passed. If your code raises an
error, read the returned traceback, fix the code, and try again.
